newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro-MPs want flexible rules on single currency.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs want flexible rules on single currency.

text.p: The European Parliament called on Thursday for a flexible interpretation of the rules which govern which European Union countries will qualify for Economic and Monetary Union.
Euro-MPs gave a lukewarm appraisal of two draft regulations which aim to ensure budgetary stability in the run-up to EMU.

The European Commission's proposals -- COM(96)496 -- are designed to tie in with a stability pact which European Union heads of state and government are expected to discuss when they meet in Dublin next month.
The first regulation will improve procedures for monitoring how closely European Union member states coordinate their national budgetary policies.
The second will clarify the rules for sanctioning member states which register excessive budget deficits.
Euro-MPs gave the draft texts a first reading (under the cooperation procedure) but said they needed improving.

"The proposed rules are inflexible, lack creative imagination and do not provide for mechanisms for positive intervention to support the convergence efforts made," Greek Christian Democrat Efthymios Christodoulou said in a report.
Parliament called for a clearer definition of excessive deficit, saying national budget policies could not be judged on arithmetic criteria alone.
It was also important to take into account the impact of these policies on employment and inflation, Euro-MPs said.
"National budgetary policies need also to be set so as to allow adequate government investment to help sustain growth and employment," said the report.
This sentiment was echoed in a second report by British Socialist Lyndon Harrison on the effects of monetary policies on the real economy.
Parliament approved three other reports on issues relating to the introduction of the single European currency, following a wide-ranging debate on the euro on Wednesday.

In response to the European Monetary Institute's recent statement that most member states currently failed to meet the convergence criteria for participating in EMU, parliament recommended a more flexible interpretation of the rules (Metten report).

Euro-MPs called for practical measures to ensure the success of the switch to a single currency in 1999, including pricing goods in both euros and national currencies during a three-year transition phase (Hoppenstedt report).

They also approved a draft regulation -- COM(96)499 -- which will prevent parties to contracts agreed in national currencies from trying to rescind or renegotiate the deals once the euro is introduced (Herman report).
